name: Bouni-Bobe
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Only Miller 2017 subclassification cited on Glottolog; no description of Bouni-Bobe (Skou) phonology located.

new_statements.quote: In Sumo, a language of the Piore River branch of the family, the following appear to be the governing conditions (the Sumo data is less well documented than the Puare or Skou data): there are five underlying tone melodies, L, H, LH, HL and LHL; the sequence *LHL may not be realised on a single syllable, but only spread over multiple syllables in such a way that there is no rise phonologically associated with a single syllable (this limits the number of contrasts on monosyllables to four); with complex tones there is an additional contrast in the placement of an accent in the word, anywhere in the final two syllables of the phonological word.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Sumo (= Bouni) is a word-tone language with five lexical melodies (L, H, LH, HL, LHL) associated at the level of the phonological word; on top of the melody, words with complex (contour) melodies contrast in the position of a phonological 'accent' (the inflection point where the melody is anchored), which may fall on either of the last two syllables of the phonological word. Accent placement is therefore lexically contrastive within a final two-syllable window, not fixed and not a separate stress system.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent is contrastive only with complex (non-level) melodies; Donohue flags the Sumo data as less well documented than Puare or Skou, and the description is a comparative excursus, not a Sumo phonology.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (accent domain notated...[σσ]# in Table 57). Data from Donohue's own survey work (Crowther, Donohue & San Roque 2000 East Coast survey), i.e. first-hand but brief. Companion data: Donohue 2003 Table 8 p.360 gives Sumo monosyllabic pitches 55, 22, 45, 51; Donohue & Crowther 2005 Table 4 p.182 gives Sumo and Nouri pitches H, L, F.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog boun1246 'Bouni-Bobe' [suo] covers two varieties: Bouni, spoken in Sumo village (Donohue's 'Sumo'; Miller 2017 p.4 'Bouni is spoken in Sumo'; Donohue 2010 tree key 'So = Sumo'), and Bobe, once spoken in Nouri village (Donohue's 'Nouri'; extinct village, speakers now in Onei, Sumo, Sera/Sarai). The quoted statement is for Sumo = Bouni only. For Nouri = Bobe the only prosodic information found is Donohue & Crowther 2005 Table 4 p.182 (pitches H, L, F; nasalisation), and Donohue 2010 p.1 notes Nouri's subgrouping is unclear (Serra Hills vs Piore River). Not to be confused with Bauni = Barupu/Warapu [bpe/wra1302] or Uni = Ramo [uni].

sources.note: p.68: Sumo (= Bouni) has five underlying tone melodies L, H, LH, HL, LHL; *LHL cannot sit on one syllable (four monosyllabic contrasts); 'with complex tones there is an additional contrast in the placement of an accent in the word, anywhere in the final two syllables of the phonological word'; Table 57 gives Sumo accent domain...[σσ]#, accent co-occurring with LH, HL, LHL. Caveat in the same sentence: 'the Sumo data is less well documented than the Puare or Skou data'.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2003. The tonal system of Skou, New Guinea. In S. Kaji (ed.), Proceedings of the symposium Cross-linguistic Studies of Tonal Phenomena, 329-365. Tokyo: ILCAA.
sources.note: Appendix 2, Table 8 (p.360): Sumo monosyllabic pitch contrasts 55 'high', 22 'low', 45 'rising', 51 'falling'. Accent-in-final-two-syllables claim is made there only for Skou and Puare, not Sumo.
Zero descriptive references; subclassification comment cites Miller 2017; AES moribund.

sources.citation: Miller, Steve A. 2017. Skou languages near Sissano Lagoon, Papua New Guinea. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 35: 1-24.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey; sec. 1.3 Bouni ('spoken in Sumo'), 1.4 Bobe (Nouri), 2.4 Bobe mutually intelligible with Bouni. Only tone remarks: Uni of Oro Toma 'said to use tone' (p.5); App. B 'Uni has at least two tones... Bauni has more'. Nothing on Bouni/Bobe stress.
